title: Guideline: fortification of food-grade salt with iodine for the prevention and control of iodine deficiency disorders
funder: WHO thanks the Government of Luxembourg and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation for financial support; the Micronutrient Initiative supports the WHO Evidence and Programme Guidance Unit for the commissioning of systematic reviews.
result: All food-grade salt used in household and food processing should be fortified with iodine (strong recommendation); evidence quality moderate for goitre and cretinism, low for cognitive function. Suggested iodine addition ranges from 65 mg/kg salt at an intake of 3 g salt/day to 39 mg/kg at 5 g/day, 20 mg/kg at 10 g/day and 14 mg/kg at 14 g/day, based on 150 µg iodine/day, 30% losses before consumption and 92% bioavailability. Salt iodisation and reduction of salt to less than 5 g/day are compatible.
